claims.text: Post-process deep cryogenic treatment will improve the dimensional precision of additively manufactured high-entropy-alloy components.
Post-process deep cryogenic treatment will improve the mechanical integrity of additively manufactured high-entropy-alloy components.
Post-process deep cryogenic treatment will reduce fabrication-induced defects in additively manufactured high-entropy-alloy components.
As-fabricated laser-additively-manufactured HfNbTaTiZr components exhibit residual stress, incomplete phase development, porosity, and micro-cracking.
The DCT intervention consists of immersing as-built components in liquid nitrogen at approximately -196 °C for an optimized duration.
DCT can be applied as a post-processing treatment after laser melting deposition of HfNbTaTiZr-family alloys.
The proposed DCT protocol is also applicable after selective laser melting and under ambient pressure.
A room-temperature recovery stage should follow DCT to stabilize the induced phase changes.
DCT induces a phase transition in additively manufactured BCC HfNbTaTiZr-family alloy.
DCT forms beneficial HCP precipitates at grain boundaries.
DCT relieves residual stress and consequently lowers the density of dislocations and pore-type defects.
DCT produces beneficial lattice distortions and controlled grain-boundary phase transitions.
DCT-induced precipitates pin defects and thereby limit the propagation or formation of fabrication-induced defects.
Relief of additive-manufacturing residual stress reduces dimensional distortion.
Relative to as-deposited Hf0.25NbTa0.25TiZr, DCT increases tensile strength by approximately 11%, consistent with the predicted roughly 10–25% range.

Relative to as-deposited Hf0.25NbTa0.25TiZr, DCT increases elongation by approximately 10%, while the reported increase relative to as-cast material is 48%, consistent with the predicted 10–50% range.
DCT-treated HEA parts will have a lower defect density than untreated as-built parts.
The intervention should be most effective in HEAs having phase-transformation kinetics similar to those of LMD-processed HfNbTaTiZr-family alloy.
Alloy system, component geometry, additive-manufacturing parameters, and DCT duration may alter or limit the improvements.
Failure to obtain statistically significant improvements in dimensional precision, tensile strength, ductility, and defect density relative to an untreated control would falsify the hypothesis.
